title: LoopTitan: What Does Parameter Revisit Buy a Mixture-of-Experts?
summary: The technique replaces a standard MoE with a looped variant that revisits the same layer parameters across depths to add effective depth at fixed parameter count; the paper's matched controls show the revisit mechanism itself contributes essentially nothing, and it proposes a standard-MoE baseline (LoopTitan-Base) that uses better network shape and the Muon optimizer instead. For the reader, adopting a looped MoE costs implementation complexity in the training/serving stack (custom recurrence, residual-scale logic) with no measured quality benefit over the non-revisit control at matched budgets, though the released pretrained LoopTitan-Base checkpoints and the Muon-plus-depth recipe are directly reusable. What can fail: the residual-scale trick only helps under AdamW's uneven per-layer step sizes and disappears under Muon, the 90.2% recovery figure leaves a residual gap that may matter at larger scales than tested, and results come from the authors' own pretraining setup so they may not transfer to downstream fine-tuning workloads on constrained hardware.
rationale: The paper's own ablations show parameter revisit adds no independent benefit, and all real gains (network shape, Muon optimizer, added compute) are transferable to a standard MoE without the looped implementation complexity.

claims.statement: The technique replaces a standard MoE with a looped variant that revisits the same layer parameters across depths to add effective depth at fixed parameter count; the paper's matched controls show the revisit mechanism itself contributes essentially nothing, and it proposes a standard-MoE baseline (LoopTitan-Base) that uses better network shape and the Muon optimizer instead. For the reader, adopting a looped MoE costs implementation complexity in the training/serving stack (custom recurrence, residual-scale logic) with no measured quality benefit over the non-revisit control at matched budgets, though the released pretrained LoopTitan-Base checkpoints and the Muon-plus-depth recipe are directly reusable. What can fail: the residual-scale trick only helps under AdamW's uneven per-layer step sizes and disappears under Muon, the 90.2% recovery figure leaves a residual gap that may matter at larger scales than tested, and results come from the authors' own pretraining setup so they may not transfer to downstream fine-tuning workloads on constrained hardware.

At equal parameters and compute, a deeper standard (non-looped) MoE under Muon recovers 90.2% of the quality gain that one extra parameter-revisit pass provides; the proposed LoopTitan-Base baseline matches the strongest looped recipe without revisit or residual scaling.
